title: When Dynamics Shift, Robust Task Inference Wins: Offline Imitation Learning with Behavior Foundation Models Revisited
claim: Methods sharing one pretrained model differ only in task inference; robust inference yields policies that degrade less under dynamics shift.
layout: 3 colored panels, left-to-right (A→B→C), latent sphere in middle, result plot at right
description: Three rounded panels, colored blue, green and purple and lettered A to C, run left to right. Panel A, Pretraining, shows unlabeled exploratory trajectories with {(s,a,s')} written under them. An arrow leads to a BFM box holding a small neural network and the labels B(s), F(s,a,z) and π_z(s). Panel B, Task-Inference, draws a green sphere standing for the latent space Z. A warm-start vector z_w sits at the top. Black jagged paths run from it to three star markers, z_FB-IL (cyan), z_RBFM-L (pink) and z_RBFM-H (lavender). A legend underneath names each star. Panel C, Performance, is a line plot of return against change in gravity (%) for RBFM-Heavy, FB-IL and RBFM-Light, with shaded confidence bands. Purple arrows point out that the proposed methods degrade less. A conclusion sentence sits at the bottom. The eye goes first to the sphere and the plot.
caption: Overview of our proposed Robust-BFM approach: All FB-IL (standard BFM), RBFM-Light (ours), and RBFM-Heavy (ours) share the same pretraining procedure, with difference arising in the task-inference stage. Policies inferred by our approach are more resilient to dynamics perturbation.
abstract: Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) enable scalable imitation learning (IL) by pretraining task-agnostic representations that can be rapidly adapted to new tasks. However, existing BFMs assume fixed environment dynamics, limiting their robustness under real-world shifts such as changes in friction, actuation, or sensor noise. We address this by formulating BFM task-inference as a robust minimax optimization problem, enabling adaptation to worst-case dynamics perturbations without modifying pretraining. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first BFM-based framework that achieves robustness to dynamics shifts while relying solely on offline data from a single nominal environment. Our approach significantly outperforms standard BFM and robust offline IL baselines under dynamics shifts. These results demonstrate that robust policy can be achieved entirely at task-inference time, improving the practicality of BFMs in dynamic settings.
